approved_text: (1) Is there k > 2 such that the k-subsets of {1,…,2k} can be (k+1)-coloured so that every (k+1)-subset contains k-subsets of all colours? (2) For every k ≥ 3, is the chromatic number of the Johnson graph J(2k,k) (k-subsets, adjacent when sharing k−1 elements) at least k+2?
draft:
Two questions:

1. Does some k > 2 allow colouring the k-subsets of {1,...,2k} with k+1 colours so that, for every (k+1)-subset A, all k+1 colours appear among A's k-subsets?

2. For every k ≥ 3, is the chromatic number of the Johnson graph J(2k,k) at least k+2? (Its vertices are k-subsets; two are adjacent when they share k−1 elements.)
source_docstrings:
Does there exist a $k>2$ such that the $k$-sized subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with
$k+1$ colours such that for every $A\subset \{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k+1$ all $k+1$
colours appear among the $k$-sized subsets of $A$?

Is the chromatic number of `J(2 * k, k)` always at least `k + 2`?
source_lean:
theorem erdos_835 : (∃ k > 2, Property k) ↔ answer(sorry)

theorem johnson_chromaticNumber : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ k ≥ 3, k + 2 ≤ J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber
